What do these mean? ▾
Document size
Segment count. Shows corpus composition — which documents are physically the largest. Useful as a baseline but doesn’t reflect policy importance.
Graph degree
Connection count within the current similarity range. This is reactive — drag the sliders and watch nodes resize in real time.
Betweenness centrality
Surfaces documents that bridge between otherwise disconnected policy clusters. High-centrality documents are the connective tissue — e.g. if you want to trace how climate policy connects to water regulation, the largest nodes here are the path.
Segment links
Cross-document text overlap at the paragraph level. Rewards substantive textual alignment rather than just thematic proximity — documents that share specific policy language or provisions, not just broad topics.
Weighted degree
Sum of similarity scores for all connections. Rewards documents that are both broadly connected and strongly connected. Highlights comprehensive documents that touch every domain at high similarity.
3D labels: the most important nodes by this metric are labelled; hover any node for its name.
